full_judgment:
Abdur Rahman Chowdhury, J.-This Rule is directed against the judgment and order passed by the Sessions Judge, Jessore, setting aside the order of acquittal passed by a Summary Martial Law Court and directing re-trial of the accused petitioner by the senior Special Judge. We have heard the learned Counsel for the petitioner and the learned Deputy Attorney General for the State. It is not necessary to set out the facts in details of this case since all the facts are admitted. The only question that calls for consideration in this Rule is whether after lifting of the Martial Law by the proclamation dated April 7, 1979 the Sessions Judge as the reviewing authority had jurisdiction to interfere with the proceeding of a Summary Martial law Court. 

 2. In the instant case Martial Law was withdrawn according to the proclamation with effect from 8 P.M. on the 6th day of April, 1979. The Criminal Case out of which the present Rule arose was admittedly pending for trial before the Summary Martial Law Court, The trial commenced before the lifting of the Martial Law and some of the P.Ws. were examined on 28.3.79 and the rest Of the P.Ws. on 7.4.79 and the petitioner was acquitted of the charges on 9.4.79. The trial in the instant case, it appears, commenced before the lifting of the Martial Law but the final, order was passed on 9.4.79 after the Martial Law was lifted. The records were sent to the' Sessions Judge, Jessore, in accordance with the Martial Law Regulation on 16.5.79 and by order dated 18.5.79 the learned Sessions Judge set aside the order of acquittal and on the ground that it had no jurisdiction to pass the impugned order after the withdrawal of the Martial Law and directed re-trial of the case in accordance with the normal law of the land. The petitioner has challenged the order passed by the Sessions Judge on the ground that it was passed without jurisdiction inasmuch as after the withdrawal of the Martial Law on 6.4.79 the Sessions Judge had no jurisdiction to pass the impugned order. Under clause (f) of the Proclamation dated April 7, 1979 it was laid down as follows: 

 "(f) the proceeding of every case tried and disposed of at any time before the commencing day by a Summary Martial law Court shall, after the commencing day, be reviewed by the Sessions Judge, hereinafter referred to as the reviewing authority, as if the said Martial Law Regulations and Martial Law Orders had not been repealed." 

 The instant case admittedly was disposed of after the commencing day, namely, April 7, 1979 and the Sessions Judge retained his authority and jurisdiction over cases which were tried and disposed of before the commencing day. We have therefore, no hesitation in holding that the impugned order passed by the Sessions Judge directing re-trial of the accused cannot be sustained in law. 

 In the result, the impugned order dated 18.5.79 passed by the Sessions Judge in Criminal Misc. Case No. 236 of 1979 (Review) is hereby set aside. The Rule is accordingly made absolute.
